Illustrative composite persona: not a real person or a real quote

Meet “Sam”: weeks off one foot, and both hands taken

Who is injured

Sam is an illustrative adult with a broken right ankle in a cast, told to keep weight off that foot for weeks. Sam lives alone, works at a desk and has stairs at home. On standard crutches, both hands are busy: carrying a mug, cooking or opening a door gets hard.

Where it hurts

A hands-free knee crutch frees the hands, but its cuff is one size fits all. The friction is where the leg meets the device: pressure on the shin and knee, straps that dig in, and fiddly donning. Hands, wrists, shoulders and the good leg also take strain from other aids.

Who operates Rehab AI

Sam can describe their day and enter tape measurements. A technician or clinician (for example at an orthotic lab) runs the engineering view, reviews every check and decides whether to approve a nonhuman fit sample. The certified commercial crutch still carries the load.

4Measure your injured leg

Use a soft tape measure, sitting with your knee bent. Measure around the calf just below the knee, then 7.5 cm lower, then 15 cm lower. Then measure the shin from the knee crease to the ankle bone, and the width across the knee. Ask someone to help if you can.
